title: Beyond Language Specialization: A RAG Evaluation of Italian LLMs
subtitle: An empirical benchmark investigating retrieval-augmented generation robustness, domain specialization, and context distraction in open Italian language models.

media.caption: Figure: Overview of the multi-stage evaluation pipeline for Italian Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

corpus.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has rapidly become the standard approach for grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) in domain-specific external knowledge. While massive multilingual models and English-centric benchmarks receive extensive attention, their behavior when deployed in localized, morphologically rich languages such as Italian remains insufficiently explored.

In this paper, we systematically evaluate open-weight Italian language models across retrieval-augmented generation workflows. We investigate whether models trained specifically for language specialization retain robustness when challenged by noisy distractors, long context documents, and cross-domain retrieval queries.
Why Language Specialization Is Not Enough

Specialized Italian LLMs demonstrate strong generative fluency and native grammatical competence. However, our experiments reveal that language adaptation during pre-training does not automatically translate into effective information synthesis under retrieval noise.

corpus.caption: Video 1: Walkthrough of retrieval noise sensitivity and context distraction across tested models.

corpus.text: Across multiple query categories spanning legal, technical, and general-domain Italian texts, our evaluation uncovered three primary phenomena:

items: Lexical vs. Semantic Recall: Italian-adapted embeddings achieve higher precision on domain-specific vocabulary, but struggle when queries involve colloquial phrasing.
Lost in the Context: When the retrieved chunk is buried in the middle of multiple passages, performance degrades by up to 28% compared to top-positioned context.
Hallucination Sensitivity: Prompt templates preserving Italian formal honorifics significantly reduced ungrounded assertions compared to direct English translations.

corpus.text: Our findings underscore the need for dedicated RAG benchmarks beyond English. In future iterations, we aim to investigate agentic retrieval mechanisms where models iteratively critique and refine retrieved evidence.
